draft.text:
{"letter":"Dear Dana Whitfield,

I've been a hockey fan my whole life, and these days I play in a weekly adult league here in Nashville. So a role telling Summit City Hockey Club's story to fans, and helping grow youth hockey along the way, caught my attention right away.

For the past five years I've run social media and events for community sports organizations. Since 2021 I've been the Social Media Manager at Riverbend Youth Soccer League, where I grew our Instagram following from 2,400 to 9,100 in two seasons. One change that made a real difference was shifting budget toward player-made video, which cut our paid ad spend by 38%. Your posting puts a lot of weight on behind-the-scenes video from games, practices and community events, and I like that focus. Real people and real moments are what fans want to see. I'd be excited to bring that thinking to the rink and keep sharpening my own shooting and editing skills while I'm at it.

Events are the other half of my work. At Riverbend I planned and ran a 40-team spring tournament with 600 attendees. Before that, as a Marketing Assistant at Harpeth Valley Rec Center, I coordinated volunteer schedules for 25 community events a year and wrote the weekly member newsletter for 3,000 subscribers. Partnering with your community team on youth hockey events feels like a natural fit, and I'm happy to work the game nights and weekends that come with the season.

On the day-to-day side, I use Hootsuite for scheduling and Google Analytics for tracking results, so planning daily content and reporting each week on growth and engagement is work I'd be comfortable jumping into from the start.

I'd love to hear what you have planned for the season and how I could help.

Thanks for your time,
Jordan Avery"}
